titolo: Zelensky vs Trump: 'He Can't Be a Friend' — Putin Row Explodes
angolo: A two-word edit to a NATO statement, a photo captioned 'My Friend', and a BBC interview in Kyiv: how three days exposed the widening gap between Zelensky and Trump.
descrizione: Zelensky vs Trump: 'He Can't Be a Friend' — Putin Row Explodes. Ukraine's president told the BBC it was 'strange' for Trump to call Putin 'my friend', and said the US is too focused on the Middle East. The same week, Trump reworded a joint NATO statement to add 'Ukraine' to a warning first aimed only at Russia. Here is what is confirmed, what is only reported, and what each side says. Sources: BBC, CBS, RTE, Kyiv Post, Interfax-Ukraine, Reuters.

scene.testo: Two words. Posted by the US president. Under a handshake: "My Friend".

grafica.sotto: Trump's caption on a photo with Putin

scene.testo: The man being invaded answered, in an interview with the BBC, from Kyiv.
"He can't be a friend."
Can Ukraine's president criticize Trump openly and still keep America on his side?
But first, a change to a joint statement with NATO. It added Ukraine to one warning.
Wednesday night. Mar-a-Lago, Florida. Trump hosts NATO chief Mark Rutte.
Florida is the first point on our map.
Both sides released a joint statement. Trump and Rutte described the meeting as "outstanding".
Its key line: Russia must avoid actions that "intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war".
Hours later, Trump posted his own version on Truth Social.
He added two words, "and Ukraine". His version of the warning referred to "Russia and Ukraine".

grafica.sotto: Added by Trump to the agreed text

scene.testo: A NATO official told Politico, anonymously, that the original wording was the version both sides had agreed.
That suggests, per that official, that Trump amended the statement unilaterally afterward.
Then Trump posted again on Truth Social, a follow-up to the joint statement.
He wrote that he wanted Putin to "pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe".
So which message would Kyiv hear? The edit, or the appeal to Putin?
Hold that thought. First, who is the man who had to answer?
Volodymyr Zelensky leads a country at war with Russia since 2022.
In February 2025, he had a bruising Oval Office encounter with Trump.
That is why this week's interview matters.
Wednesday, November 19. Shenzhen, China. An APEC summit.
Trump and Putin met briefly, ahead of a three-way summit with Xi Jinping.
Trump greeted Putin as a "friend", according to reports from the summit.
Days later he posted a handshake photo, captioned "My Friend".
The declaration of the trilateral summit did not directly mention Russia's war against Ukraine, according to The New Voice of Ukraine.
Back in Florida, on Thanksgiving, a reporter pressed Trump on the contrast between calling Putin a friend and urging him to stop military aggression.
Trump said: "We want to make a deal. We want to stop killing."

citazione.testo: We want to make a deal. We want to stop killing.

scene.testo: He added: "I could say he's not a friend... I want to make a deal."
He argued that hostile rhetoric would get him "absolutely nowhere", and compared it to the strained relationship between Zelensky and Putin.
He also claimed Russia is losing 25,000 people a month.
Now to Kyiv. Zelensky gave an interview to the BBC's Sarah Rainsford.
He started carefully: "Of course it's up to the president of the United States."
Then he said: "It's strange."

citazione.testo: Of course it's up to the president of the United States, but… it's strange.

scene.testo: He called Putin "an aggressor" and "a killer".
Then came the comparison that drew headlines.
He likened it to calling Hitler a good friend during World War Two.
"No, he's not a friend."
He said the US is too focused on the Middle East.
"It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more."

citazione.testo: It's a pity they made a focus on Middle East and they help them more.

scene.testo: He said delays in anti-ballistic missiles are costing Ukrainian lives, per the BBC.
Ukraine's military can now destroy about 70 percent of Russia's fastest drones, Zelensky told the BBC.
But he warned of a "very, very big" deficit of interceptors for ballistic missiles.
He said the Americans were delaying deliveries of Patriot systems.
Meanwhile, the strikes keep coming. Here is what Russia hit this week.
On Wednesday, Reuters reported outages in five regions after a Russian overnight attack.
Odesa's governor said a massive drone attack damaged civilian and energy infrastructure.
On Friday, Ukrainian officials reported strikes in nine regions, including rail and energy.
Euronews reports more than 1,000 strikes on Ukraine's energy system since September.
Moscow says it targets military-linked sites, and denies targeting civilians, Reuters has reported.
Now the envoys. Two weeks of talks, and one controversial interview.
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators met in Abu Dhabi earlier this month.
Newsweek says they agreed a major prisoner exchange, but not on territory.
Envoys Kushner and Witkoff then went to Moscow to meet Putin.
On a podcast released November 25, Kushner called Putin "definitely a grandmaster of politics".

citazione.testo: But he's definitely a grandmaster of politics.

scene.testo: He also said he and Witkoff concluded that territory is blocking an end to the war.
Kushner also said Putin has "reassured us" that using nuclear weapons is not his intention.
And Zelensky says it's unclear whether European negotiators will even be at the table.
That brings us to what happens next.
Zelensky called for "real helpful allies, who can push Russia".

citazione.testo: real helpful allies, who can push Russia

scene.testo: He urged the US to live up to its reputation as a strong country, with "power and respect".
Trump says he wants a deal. Zelensky says pressure must fall on Moscow.
Same war. Two very different views of what to say about Putin.

visivo.testo: Same war. Two very different views of what to say about Putin.
